missing.reason: All 5 vendors model an approval record on changes and high-value requests (ServiceNow sysapproval_approver, Freshservice approvals, Halo approval processes). This is the spine of change governance and the audit object for SOX/ISO20000 change control. ITSM owns service_changes but has no approval object.

Every vendor records an immutable per-ticket state/field history (ServiceNow sys_audit/activity stream, Jira changelog, Freshservice ticket activities, Halo action log). Required as the ITIL/ISO20000 evidence trail and as the source of cycle-time/MTTR analytics. No transition/history object exists today.

Task/sub-task decomposition under a parent ticket is universal (ServiceNow task table, Freshservice/ManageEngine tasks, Halo subtickets). The current footprint has flat masters with no child-work object, so multi-team incident/request work cannot be tracked.
Implementation/back-out tasks under a change are core to change execution across all suites. Distinct from incident_tasks by lifecycle (planned vs reactive). Absent today.

The persisted CAB/approver decision history (who approved, when, comments) that auditors sample for SOX change control. If ticket_approvals is modeled generically this may collapse into it; flagged so the change-approval audit trail is explicitly owned.

The Known Error Database is a first-class ITIL object distinct from problems (ServiceNow known_error, Freshservice/ManageEngine/Halo KEDB). It links a root cause to a workaround and is consumed by incident triage. ITSM owns service_problems but not the known-error record.

Major Incident Management is a packaged module in ServiceNow, Freshservice and Halo with its own record (war-room, timeline, post-incident review). Distinct lifecycle and stakeholder comms from a normal incident. Not present.

Release management is a named ITIL practice and a separate record/module in ServiceNow, Freshservice, ManageEngine and Halo, grouping multiple changes for coordinated deployment. The module is named Change and Release Management but masters only service_changes.
CAB as a standing/recurring body with membership and meeting agenda is modeled by ServiceNow, ManageEngine and Halo. Underpins the approval workflow. Absent.

Assignment/support groups (queues) are the routing primitive in every ITSM tool (ServiceNow sys_user_group as assignment_group, Freshservice/Jira teams, Halo teams). Tickets are assigned to a group before an individual. No group/queue object exists; org_units (HR) is not the support-group concept.
SLA escalation/notification policies are configured records in all five vendors and drive the SLA breach workflow. The SLA module masters service_slas but has no escalation config.
The recorded breach/at-risk event (task_sla in ServiceNow, SLA timers in others) is the measurable that feeds SLA reporting and chargeback. Distinct from the SLA definition. Not modeled.
Public/private work-notes and conversation threads on every ticket are universal (ServiceNow journal fields, Jira/Freshservice/Halo comments). The primary engagement object; absent.
CSAT/feedback on resolved tickets is a standard reporting object across all five vendors. Drives the agent-reporting module's KPI surface. Not modeled.
Knowledge taxonomy/category hierarchy is a config master in all KB implementations; articles are filed under it. The knowledge module masters articles but not their categorization.

The ordered-item line under a request (ServiceNow REQ/RITM split, ManageEngine request resources) lets one request fulfill multiple catalog items. The footprint has service_requests + service_catalog_items but no line/order-item junction connecting them at fulfillment time.
Catalog-task workflow under a request item (ServiceNow catalog tasks/SCTASK, Freshservice/ManageEngine fulfillment stages). The execution substrate of request fulfillment; absent.

On-call rotations are central to Jira Service Management (Opsgenie), ServiceNow on-call, and Freshservice. They route alerts/major incidents to the right responder. Present in the event/alert domain in every modern suite; absent here.
OLAs (internal team commitments) sit alongside SLAs in ServiceNow, ManageEngine and Halo and are tracked separately for breach attribution. The module masters service_slas only.

The impact/urgency-to-priority matrix is a configurable master in all five vendors and gates SLA timers. Could be enum-only, but ServiceNow/Freshservice/ManageEngine model it as a table. Flagged as candidate config master.

Approval-routing rules (who must approve which change/request) are configured records driving ticket_approvals; underpin segregation-of-duties. Modeled by ServiceNow, Freshservice, ManageEngine, Halo.
Scheduled maintenance/blackout windows constrain when changes may execute (ServiceNow maintenance schedules, Freshservice/ManageEngine). Tied to change scheduling and collision detection.
Article helpful/not-helpful ratings and flagged-for-review feedback (ServiceNow, Freshservice, Halo) drive KB quality. Engagement object on the knowledge master; absent.
Shift/roster definitions for support staff (ServiceNow, Jira, Halo) drive coverage and routing; weaker than agent_groups but commonly modeled. Candidate.

scope_creep.reason: Mastered by CMDB (domain 4). Held as embedded_master here, which is the correct autonomous-deployable shape (Rule #19), not creep. Listed for completeness; recommend KEEP.
Boundary object with ITOM/OBS. ITSM legitimately masters the alert as it enters the service-management workflow (event-to-incident). Within scope. KEEP.
Mastered by OBS/observability. Consumed here for incident enrichment, correct consumer role. KEEP.
Mastered by HAM. ITSM contributes lifecycle events (e.g., incident-triggered RMA). Correct contributor role. KEEP.
Likely mastered by an HR/onboarding domain; consumed here when a service request triggers onboarding fulfillment. Correct consumer. KEEP, but verify the master domain exists.
Reference master for chargeback. Embedded for autonomy. KEEP.

modularization.assessment: The 8-module split maps cleanly onto the canonical ITIL/ITSM practice areas and onto how flagship vendors package the domain (ServiceNow's Incident/Problem/Change/Request/Knowledge product split, Freshservice's modules, Halo's areas). Every module has >=1 domain-owned master (Rule #14 satisfied): INCIDENT->service_incidents, SERVICE-REQUEST->service_requests+service_catalog_items, PROBLEM->service_problems, CHANGE->service_changes, EVENT->monitoring_alerts, KNOWLEDGE->knowledge_articles, SLA->service_slas, AGENT-WORKSPACE is the cross-cutting reporting/queue surface. A first-time deployer would self-explain all eight names. The gaps are entity-level (workflow substrate: approvals, tasks, history, groups, escalations) NOT module-level. No merges/splits/renames required; two cosmetic notes below.

recommendations.reason: Module boundaries are correct and vendor-aligned. The fix is filling each module's workflow substrate, not restructuring.

AGENT-WORKSPACE currently has zero domain-owned masters of its own (only embedded org_units/locations). Per Rule #14 a module needs >=1 master. The MISSING entities agent_groups, ticket_state_transitions, ticket_comments, ticket_priorities, customer_satisfaction_surveys are its natural masters; once any are added the module becomes Rule-#14-compliant. Until then it is a soft-fail (reporting/overlay module with only consumed/embedded rows). Flagged, not a rename.
Named Change and Release Management but masters only service_changes. service_releases (MISSING) is the second master that makes the name honest. Add the entity rather than rename the module.
